title: Set 126

sentences.ko: 아, 나도 그러고 싶은데 토요일에 우리 형 부엌 페인트칠 도와주기로 이미 말해 놨어. 지난번에도 형한테 약속 펑크 냈거든. 이번에 또 그러면 두고두고 그 얘기 들을 거야. 그래도 일요일에 일손이 더 필요하면 점심 먹고 들를 수 있어.
sentences.text: Ah, I wish I could, but I already told my brother I'd help him paint his kitchen on Saturday, and I bailed on him last time, so if I do it again he's never going to let me hear the end of it. If you still need an extra pair of hands on Sunday, though, I can come by after lunch.

alts.text: Man, I can't. Promised my brother I'd help paint his kitchen Saturday, and I flaked on him last time, so if I do it again he'll never let it go. Still need a hand Sunday? I can swing by after lunch.

I am afraid I cannot, as I have already promised my brother that I would help him paint his kitchen on Saturday. I let him down the last time, and if I were to do so again, he would never let me forget it. However, if you still require assistance on Sunday, I would be glad to come by after lunch.

sentences.note: **bailed on** 는 사람과의 약속을 막판에 펑크 낸다는 뜻이에요. **never going to let me hear the end of it** 는 두고두고 그 얘기를 꺼낼 거라는 말이고, **an extra pair of hands** 는 일손 하나 더를 말해요.

sentences.ko: 너희 딸도 그 과학 과제 해? 우리 딸은 화산을 골랐길래 잘했다고 했지. 근데 어젯밤 아홉 시에 와서는 목요일까지 내야 하고 포스터 보드가 필요하대. 그래서 밤 열 시에 드러그스토어에 누가 가 있었게? 지난주에만 말해 줬어도 기꺼이 도와줬을 텐데.
sentences.text: Is your daughter doing that science project too? Because mine picked volcanoes, and I said great, and then last night at nine she tells me it's due Thursday and she needs a poster board. So guess who was at the drugstore at ten? I'd have been happy to help if she'd just told me last week.

alts.text: Wait, your daughter's got that science project too? Mine went with volcanoes, fine, great, then at nine last night she goes, oh, it's due Thursday and I need a poster board. So guess who's at the drugstore at ten? I'd have happily helped if she'd just said something last week.

Is your daughter also working on that science project? My daughter chose volcanoes, which I was pleased about, but last night at nine o'clock she informed me that it is due on Thursday and that she needs a poster board. As a result, I was at the drugstore at ten. I would have been glad to help had she told me last week.

sentences.note: **guess who** 는 누구였게? 하고 물은 뒤 결국 나였다고 푸념할 때 써요. **it's due Thursday** 는 목요일까지 내야 한다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 아니야, 여기는 다 괜찮아. 차 문제는 해결됐으니까 이제 걱정 안 해도 돼. 목소리가 좀 이상하게 들리면 방금 낮잠 자다 깨서 그래, 그게 다야. 그건 그렇고 아빠 무릎은 좀 어때?
sentences.text: Yeah, no, everything's good here. The car thing got sorted out, so you can stop worrying about that. If I sound a little off, it's because I just woke up from a nap, that's all. Anyway, how's Dad's knee doing?

alts.text: Nah, all good over here. Car stuff's sorted, so quit worrying about it. If I sound kinda weird, I just woke up from a nap, that's it. So how's Dad's knee?

Everything is fine here. The matter with the car has been resolved, so there is no need to worry about it any longer. If I sound slightly unlike myself, it is only because I have just woken from a nap. In any case, how is Father's knee?

sentences.note: **Yeah, no** 는 상대 말을 받으면서 아니라고 할 때 쓰는 입말이에요. **got sorted out** 는 문제가 해결됐다는 뜻이고, **a little off** 는 평소와 좀 다르다는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

sentences.ko: 드디어 치과에 갔는데, 알고 보니 내가 자면서 이를 갈고 있었대. 그래서 매일 아침 턱이 아팠나 봐. 의사가 밤에 마우스피스를 끼라는데 그 말 듣고 좀 웃었어. 안 그래도 침대에서 편하게 눕기가 힘든데 말이야.
sentences.text: So I finally went to the dentist, and apparently I've been grinding my teeth in my sleep, which would explain why my jaw's been sore every morning. He wants me to wear a mouth guard at night, and I kind of laughed, because I can't get comfortable in bed as it is.

alts.text: Finally made it to the dentist, and turns out I grind my teeth in my sleep, so that's why my jaw's sore every morning. He wants me in a mouth guard at night, and I kinda laughed, since I can't get comfy in bed as it is.

I finally visited the dentist, and it appears that I have been grinding my teeth while I sleep, which would account for the soreness in my jaw every morning. He would like me to wear a mouth guard at night, and I must admit I laughed, because I already find it difficult to get comfortable in bed.

sentences.note: **apparently** 는 들어 보니 ~래 하고 전해 들은 것을 말할 때 써요. **grinding my teeth** 는 이를 간다는 뜻이고, **as it is** 는 안 그래도, 지금도 이미라는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 어젯밤에 애 재우는 데 한 시간 반 걸렸어. 잠들었나 싶어서 몰래 방을 빠져나가려고 하면 꼭 바닥이 삐걱거리고, 그러면 애가 벌떡 일어나 앉아서 어디 가냐고 물어. 진짜 잠들었을 때는 내가 너무 녹초가 돼서 애 방 바닥에 삼십 분을 더 누워 있었어. 도저히 몸이 안 일으켜지더라.
sentences.text: It took me an hour and a half to get him down last night. Every time I thought he was out, I'd try to sneak out of the room and the floor would creak, and he'd sit straight up and ask where I was going. By the time he actually fell asleep I was so wiped that I just lay there on his floor for another half hour, because I couldn't make myself get up.

alts.text: Took me an hour and a half to get him to sleep last night. Every time I thought he was out, I'd tiptoe to the door, the floor would creak, and boom, he's sitting up asking where I'm going. By the time he actually conked out I was so wiped I just lay on his floor another half hour. Couldn't make myself get up.

Last night it took me an hour and a half to get him to sleep. Each time I believed he had fallen asleep, I attempted to leave the room quietly, but the floor would creak, and he would sit straight up and ask where I was going. By the time he finally fell asleep, I was so exhausted that I remained lying on his floor for another half hour, because I could not bring myself to get up.

sentences.note: **get him down** 는 아이를 재운다는 뜻이에요. **wiped** 는 완전히 녹초가 됐다는 말이고, **couldn't make myself get up** 는 일어나려고 해도 몸이 말을 안 들었다는 뜻이에요.

reviewed: 2번 한국어: 포스터 보드를 사러 간 미국 drugstore를 약국이라고 하면 한국 사람에게는 어색해서 드러그스토어로 바꿨다
4번 한국어: I kind of laughed는 내가 웃었다는 말인데 좀 웃겼어는 상황이 우스웠다는 뜻이라 그 말 듣고 좀 웃었어로 고쳤다
5번 casual: sneak for the door는 원어민이 잘 안 쓰는 조합이라 tiptoe to the door로 바꿨다
